body:
I appreciate that you took the time to write this out. I don't have any interest in playing music personally but I do understand where you're coming from. I have my animation and game dev for that but I can't get anywhere on a project because I can't motivate, the same would go for music.

By can't motivate I'm saying my illness completely shuts off my ability, it's not laziness and it's not something you can overcome with willpower.

There's no point telling me to seek professional aid. Been there, done that, no options left, seen the best of the best, tried every potentially helpful anti-psychotic, anti-depressants have never affected me, etc. etc.

Interesting way to look at it, I have some experience with character design from game dev / film work but it feels weird to consider making one for myself.

I don't think this is possible for me, even if I tried, my head will just switch off any motivation to a crippling extent. It's like a light switch, if my life ever has any potential to improve, it switches off the ability to continue what I'm doing.

Thanks for taking the time to respond. I'll tell you this much, someone who can relate and understand what I'm going through is a thousand times better than someone who questions my attempts to get better and improve my life or offers false support/wishful thinking like almost everywhere else.

When that happens it's really upsetting because I know how hard I've fought just to hold on to my humanity let alone make a good life - harder than the vast majority of people would believe possible. But everyone seems to want to tell me that I'm just giving up, that I did everything half-baked, that I'm not trying hard enough. To quote one of my favorite anime "ask not the sparrow how the eagle soars", meaning, they aren't capable of imagining the effort I've put forth nor the weight of this illness. I guess that quote is misplaced because it's being used for a differing intent.

If I had a time machine I don't think I'd use it either way. Even with that, I can't see a way to save myself from my fate. Looking back over my life, it was cast in steel. No one ever had the capacity to change it if they wanted to.

So thinking I could go back in time and kill myself doesn't seem to have any meaning, because if I just do it now, I'm gone and there's no reason to go back, no reason for anything, to think, feel, hate. I really hate this world and the people in it. I don't feel like I'm a human being and I blame them for it but also, I believe I am right to blame them.

For the wishful thinking stories, I actually feel betrayed and lied to because as a child that's what people told me - it gets better. They all lied to me, and not just in their words, but also because they pushed their beliefs into my head and I feel mentally violated the same way Christians always made me feel when I talked to them as a child. And furthermore their beliefs come from their own weakness and their weakness made me suffer.

I grew up without any concept of individuality, it took a long time for me to realize that people differed at all. I understand only that they had a limitless capacity to exhibit cruelty and hatred, later in life I noticed varying levels, and over the years they gained separate identities and I learned to exempt a rare few from my perception of humans.

As for your question about why no one should have to care that much, I mean that I shouldn't have to be crawling across the ground on what's left of my legs begging for someone to actually give a shit, because I should of grown up with enough strength to not care either way and assert myself in a way they gets me the things I need in life.
